body.heading: The ordinary is most of life
paragraphs: Birthdays, holidays, and achievements make up a handful of days a year. The rest is Tuesdays: commutes, dinners, small talk, sleep. A gratitude practice that only works on special days misses nearly all of your life.

Ordinary gratitude is not about pretending everything is wonderful. It is about noticing that inside an unremarkable day there are usually a few unremarkable mercies: hot water, a working car, someone who laughed at your joke.

body.heading: A practice that fits in a minute
paragraphs: At one regular moment — brushing your teeth, locking up, the drive home — name three ordinary things from the day that were good. Keep them small on purpose; small is where most good things live.
Say one of them out loud to whoever provided it, when you can. Gratitude kept private is a fine practice; gratitude delivered is a relationship.

description: It is easy to be grateful at milestones. The practice that changes a life is gratitude for Tuesdays.
